description: A solid refined wax that is shredded and melted into oil to thicken a leather dressing. On its own it would stiffen leather, but blended with oil it contributes body to a preservative that stays soft and non-tacky.
name: paraffin wax

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XXII, p.302. Internet Archive.
